title: Entropy Dynamics Do Not Provide Reliable Execution-Free Selection Signals for Code Generation

contributions.purpose: Establish whether entropy-dynamics instability signals transfer from math reasoning to execution-free best-of-N code selection.
contributions.mechanism: Adapts EDIS to code generation as nEDIS (normalized EDIS with length/scale normalization) and tests it against pre-registered success criteria with statistical significance testing.
contributions.evaluation: Negative result: nEDIS fails the pre-registered criterion, underperforming random first-sample selection by 12.8-27.5pp on HumanEval and MBPP (nEDIS_v2 56.1%/41.5% vs random 68.9%/69.0%; fails to beat length-only on MBPP, 41.5% vs 66.4%, p=1.0).
contributions.source_quote: We provide a rigorous negative result showing that entropy dynamics do not transfer from math reasoning to code generation, with pre-registered success criteria and statistical significance testing.

contributions.purpose: Explain why spike-based entropy detection fails for instruction-tuned code models.
contributions.mechanism: Identifies entropy sparsity as the failure mode: per-token entropy values are overwhelmingly exactly zero due to high model confidence, undermining EDIS's spike-detection mechanism.
contributions.evaluation: 88.3% of per-token entropy values are exactly zero with instruction-tuned code models; optimization needed to improve nEDIS contradicts the original hypothesis, suggesting length bias rather than meaningful entropy dynamics.
contributions.source_quote: We identify entropy sparsity as a fundamental failure mode: instruction-tuned code models are highly confident on most tokens, undermining the spike-detection mechanism that EDIS relies on.

contributions.purpose: Prevent duplicated wasted effort and enable follow-up research on execution-free selection.
contributions.mechanism: Public release of the code and data from the nEDIS experiments.
contributions.evaluation: Code released at gitlab.com/fars-a/edis-code-bestofn; no separate quantitative evaluation.
contributions.source_quote: We release our code and data to prevent others from pursuing this direction and to enable future research on alternative execution-free selection methods.

self_declared_provenance.quote: To test this hypothesis rigorously, we adapt EDIS to code generation as nEDIS (Normalized EDIS), introducing length and scale normalizations appropriate for variable-length code.
Our work tests whether EDIS-style entropy dynamics transfer to code generation.
Unlike these approaches, we test whether entropy dynamics alone can provide selection signals without any training or execution feedback.

notes: Explicit negative-result paper: nEDIS and all entropy-based variants underperform trivial baselines (random first-sample, length-only selection); pre-registered success criterion failed.
